references.text: Isaiah prophesies that the stars, sun, and moon will not give their light – cosmic signs heralding the Lord's day. This is the background for Jesus' words about signs in the sun, moon, and stars ([ref:Jes 13:10|Isaiah 13:10]).
Isaiah describes how the entire host of heaven will wither away, and the heavens will be rolled up like a scroll – cosmic upheavals linked to God's judgment ([ref:Jes 34:4|Isaiah 34:4]).
Joel prophesies about signs in the sky and on earth before the coming of the Lord's great and dreadful day – the sun turned to darkness and the moon to blood ([ref:Joel 2:30-31|Joel 2:30-31]).
Joel again describes how the sun and moon will be darkened and the stars lose their brightness, as cosmic signs of God's judgment ([ref:Joel 3:15|Joel 3:15]).
The psalmist describes how nations rage and gather in fear when God displays His power – parallel to "the distress of nations" in Luke 21:25 ([ref:Sal 65:8|Psalms 65:8]).
Isaiah describes that the moon will be put to shame and the sun ashamed, for the Lord will reign on Mount Zion – cosmic signs linked to God's final dominion ([ref:Jes 24:23|Isaiah 24:23]).
In Matthew's parallel account, Jesus describes how the sun will be darkened, the moon lose its light, and the stars fall – the synoptic parallel to Luke 21:25 ([ref:Matt 24:29|Matthew 24:29]).
Mark's parallel account of end-time signs: the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven ([ref:Mark 13:24-25|Mark 13:24-25]).

In Revelation, cosmic signs are described when the sixth seal is broken: a great earthquake, the sun turned black, the moon like blood, and the stars falling to earth ([ref:Åp 6:12-13|Revelation 6:12-13]).
Isaiah describes the roaring of nations like the roaring sea – an image parallel to the roaring of the sea and the distress of nations in Luke 21:25 ([ref:Jes 17:12-13|Isaiah 17:12-13]).

The psalmist describes that even if the earth changes and the mountains shake in the midst of the sea, its waters roaring and foaming, God's people need not fear – the roaring of the sea as an image of chaos and judgment ([ref:Sal 46:3-4|Psalms 46:3-4]).
